title: Differential Accessible Regions
text:
This code performs a full pipeline for extracting, sorting, indexing, and generating coverage tracks (bigWig files) from BAM files associated with single-cell multiome data, focusing on a specific cell type (“CA1-do”). Here’s a unified explanation of what it does:

It lists all BAM files in the current directory and subdirectories, filtering to keep only those paths that include “outs” (likely 10x Genomics output folders).
It loads a previously saved list of SingleCellExperiment objects (scelist), each likely corresponding to a different sample, and loads the TENxMultiomeTools package.
For each sce object in scelist, it calls createBamCt to extract reads specific to the cell type "CA1-do" using the "labels" column to define cell identities. The function saves new BAM files (cell-type specific) in 2023/bams, using the sample identifier (sce$Sample) to locate the original BAMs and determine output structure. The commented code above it suggests this step can be generalized to all cell types.
After generating these BAM files, it sorts them using samtools sort with 10 threads, saving the output with a _sorted.bam suffix.
It then indexes the sorted BAM files using samtools index with 10 threads.
Finally, for each sorted BAM, it generates a normalized coverage track in bigWig format using bamCoverage, labeling it as “GEX” or “ATAC” depending on whether the BAM filename includes “GEX”. Normalization is done using CPM (counts per million), and the results are saved under 2023/bw/.

This pipeline is tailored for preparing cell type–specific signal tracks for genome browser visualization or downstream analysis.
Note: This code chunk is not evaluated in the document to save time. We directly begin from the pre-annotated dataset, which includes the information described above.


Code
bams <- list.files(".", pattern="*bam$", recursive=TRUE, full.names=TRUE)
bams <- bams[grep("outs",bams)]
#@risso1:/mnt/tebe/drighelli/multiome_2022/preprocess_multiome/2023
scelist <- readRDS("2023/scelist_SR_dbl_signacfilt_dimred_noATAC_doublrm.RDS")
library(TENxMultiomeTools)

lapply(scelist, function(sce){
    # lapply(unique(sce$labels), function(ct){
    #     createBamCt(sce, cellType=ct, cellTypesCol="labels", 
    #         bamdir=unique(sce$Sample), outdir=paste0("2023/bams/", basename(unique(sce$Sample)), ncores=10)
    # })
    createBamCt(sce, cellType="CA1-do", cellTypesCol="labels",
        bamdir=unique(sce$Sample), outdir="2023/bams", ncores=10)
})
bams <- list.files("2023/bams", pattern="*.bam$", recursive=TRUE, full.names=TRUE)
lapply(bams, function(bam)
{
    cmd <- paste0("samtools sort -@ 10 ", bam," -o ", gsub(".bam$", "", bam), "_sorted.bam")
    print(cmd)
    system(cmd)
})
bamss <- list.files("2023/bams", pattern="*_sorted.bam$", recursive=TRUE, full.names=TRUE)
lapply(bamss, function(bam)
{
    cmd <- paste0("samtools index -b ", bam, " -@ 10 ")
    print(cmd)
    system(cmd)
})

## creating bigwigs
bams <- list.files("2023/bams", pattern="*sorted.bam$", recursive=TRUE, full.names=TRUE)
void <- lapply(bams, function(bam)
{
    prefix <- ifelse( length(grep("GEX", bam)) != 0, "GEX", "ATAC" )
    cmd <- paste0("bamCoverage --normalizeUsing CPM -b ", bam,
                " -o 2023/bw/", prefix, "_", gsub(".bam", ".bw", basename(bam)), " -p ",
                10)
    message(cmd)
    system(cmd)
})

title: Differential Expression Wild Type for CA1-do
text:
Loading required libraries


Code
library(scater)
library(edgeR)
library(RUVSeq)
library(darioscripts)
library(DT)
library(ggpubr)
source("../R/luciavolcano.R")
library(muscat)
library(biomaRt)




Pseudo-bulk data construction for differential analysis
In this code chunk, we construct pseudo-bulk RNA-seq data from single-cell multiome datasets using the TENxMultiomeTools package. Specifically, we:

Load a list of SingleCellExperiment objects (scelist) representing multiple samples.
Aggregate the single-cell count data across cell labels (using aggregateAcrossCells) to simulate bulk RNA-seq profiles for each annotated group.
Generate a combined SingleCellExperiment object (scepseudo) by merging the pseudo-bulk profiles from all samples.
Save the resulting pseudo-bulk dataset to an RDS file for downstream analysis.

This step is performed to prepare the data for differential expression analysis, which is more robust when applied to aggregated (pseudo-bulk) counts rather than single-cell counts.

Note: This code chunk is not evaluated in the document for time-saving purposes. Instead, we directly start from the pre-computed results stored in the GEX_pseudo_2023.RDS file.



Code
scelist <- readRDS("~/Downloads/multiome_data/data/scelist_SR_dbl_signacfilt_dimred_noATAC_doublrm.RDS")

library(TENxMultiomeTools)
scelistpseudo <- lapply(scelist, function(sce)
{
    scea <- aggregateAcrossCells(sce, use.assay.type="counts",
        id=DataFrame(label=sce$labels))
    colnames(scea) <- paste(scea$label, scea$replicate, scea$condition, scea$genotype, sep="_")
    scea
})

scepseudo <- cbind(scelistpseudo[[1]], scelistpseudo[[2]],scelistpseudo[[3]],scelistpseudo[[4]],
                   scelistpseudo[[5]],scelistpseudo[[6]],scelistpseudo[[7]],scelistpseudo[[8]],
                   scelistpseudo[[9]],scelistpseudo[[10]],scelistpseudo[[11]],scelistpseudo[[12]])

saveRDS(scepseudo, file="~/Downloads/multiome_data/data/GEX_pseudo_2023.RDS")




Loading and annotating pseudo-bulk data for differential analysis
In this code chunk, we load the previously computed pseudo-bulk gene expression dataset and perform sample- and gene-level annotations in preparation for differential expression analysis. The steps include:

Loading data:

The pseudo-bulk dataset is read from the RDS file GEX_pseudo_2023.RDS.
A composite variable gcondition is created by concatenating genotype and condition.
Each sample is annotated with a high-level cell class (superclass) based on the label, distinguishing non-neuronal, glutamatergic, and GABAergic neuronal populations.

Annotating negative controls:

A set of known negative control genes is loaded and split into training and testing subsets (90% and 10%, respectively).
Genes in the pseudo-bulk dataset are flagged as negative controls (negctl) or test negative controls (negctltest) accordingly.

Annotating positive controls:

Known positive control genes are loaded from an external file and flagged in the dataset (posctl).
Their presence in the dataset is also recorded in a kept column.

Filtering samples:

The dataset is restricted to samples from the wild-type (WT) genotype only.




Code
multiome <- readRDS("~/Downloads/multiome_data/data/GEX_pseudo_2023.RDS") # pseudobulk


multiome$gcondition <- paste(multiome$genotype, multiome$condition, sep="_")

multiome$superclass <- "Non Neuronal"

multiome$superclass[multiome$label %in% 
        c("CA1-do","CA1-ProS", "CA1", "CA2", "CA3", "SUB-ProS", "DG")] <- "Neuronal - Glutamatergic"
multiome$superclass[multiome$label %in% 
        c("Lamp5", "Sncg", "Vip", "Serpinf1", "Ntng1", "Pvalb", "Sst", "Sst-Chodl")] <- "Neuronal - Gabaergic"


nc <- readRDS("~/Downloads/multiome_data/ctrls/SD_neg_ctrl.RDS")

rowData(multiome)$negctl[rownames(multiome) %in% nc$symbol] <- TRUE

Annotating genes with reference metadata
In this code chunk, we enrich the pseudo-bulk dataset with gene-level annotations using an external reference table. The steps performed are:

A reference table (features_duplicates.tsv) containing gene metadata (such as gene symbols, Ensembl IDs, chromosome locations, and genomic coordinates) is loaded.
Genes in the pseudo-bulk dataset are matched with entries in the reference table based on gene symbols.
For matched genes, the following annotations are added to the rowData of the multiome object:

TENxSymbol: official 10x Genomics gene symbol
TENxEnsembl: Ensembl gene ID
TENxChr: chromosome
TENxStart: transcription start coordinate
TENxEnd: transcription end coordinate


This metadata is useful for downstream analysis and interpretation of differential expression results.


Code
feat <- read.table("~/Downloads/multiome_data/reference/features_duplicates.tsv", sep="\t", header=TRUE)
rn <- rownames(rowData(multiome)) 
idx <- which(rn %in% feat$symbol)
idx1 <- which(feat$symbol %in% rn)
rowData(multiome)$TENxSymbol[idx] <- feat$symbol[idx1]
rowData(multiome)$TENxEnsembl[idx] <- feat$ensembl[idx1]
rowData(multiome)$TENxChr[idx] <- feat$chr[idx1]
rowData(multiome)$TENxStart[idx] <- feat$start[idx1]
rowData(multiome)$TENxEnd[idx] <- feat$end[idx1]




Exploratory analysis of raw (non-normalized) data
In this code chunk, we explore the structure of the raw (non-normalized) pseudo-bulk counts for the "CA1-do" cell population using dimensionality reduction techniques:

Principal Component Analysis (PCA):

A PCA is computed on the log-transformed raw counts (log1p(counts(...))).
The PCA plot distinguishes samples by condition using different colors and shapes.
The function plotPCAs is used to generate the plot with cowplot styling, and color/shape mappings are customized.

Normalization:

Log-normalization is then applied using logNormCounts normalization to prepare the data for subsequent analyses.


This step provides a visual assessment of variability in the raw data and sets up the object for normalized downstream analyses.


Code
ca1do <- multiome[,multiome$label=="CA1-do"]
plotPCAs(log1p(counts(ca1do)),
         colData=colData(ca1do),
         shapeBy="condition",
         colorBy="condition", cowplot=TRUE, prefix="log(raw-counts) CA1-do",
         returnOnly=TRUE, size=3) +
        scale_color_manual(values=c("red", "black")) + scale_shape_manual(values = 16:17) + 
    theme_bw()

Data subsetting, upper-quartile normalization, and PCA visualization
First, we apply upper-quartile normalization to account for sequencing depth differences across samples. After normalization, we perform a PCA on the log-transformed normalized counts to visualize how samples cluster by their condition, which helps assess batch effects or biological differences.


Code
ca1do <- multiome[, multiome$labels == "CA1-do"]
uq <- EDASeq::betweenLaneNormalization(counts(ca1do), which = "upper")
plotPCAs(log1p(uq),
         colData = colData(ca1do),
         shapeBy = "condition",
         colorBy = "condition",
         cowplot = TRUE,
         prefix = "WT log(UQ)",
         returnOnly = TRUE,
         size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("red", "black")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = 16:17) +
  theme_bw()

RUVs normalization and PCA visualization
To remove unwanted variation not captured by the condition (e.g., batch effects), we apply RUVs normalization using a set of negative control genes. We define sample groups by condition and use k=3 factors to adjust. The normalized counts from RUVs are stored, and a PCA is again performed on these adjusted counts to check if unwanted variation was reduced.


Code
grp <- makeGroups(ca1do$condition)
rownames(grp) <- unique(ca1do$condition)

k <- 3
ruvs <- RUVs(x = round(as.matrix(uq)),
             cIdx = rownames(ca1do)[rowData(ca1do)$negctl],
             k = k,
             scIdx = grp,
             round = TRUE)

assays(ca1do)$uqruvsk3 <- ruvs$normalizedCounts
assays(ca1do)$loguqruvsk3 <- log1p(ruvs$normalizedCounts)

plotPCAs(log1p(ruvs$normalizedCounts),
         colData = colData(ca1do),
         shapeBy = "condition",
         colorBy = "condition",
         cowplot = TRUE,
         prefix = paste0("WT log(UQ+RUVsk", k, ")"),
         returnOnly = TRUE,
         size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("red", "black")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = 16:17) +
  theme_bw()

Add RUVs factors to sample metadata and filter genes
We append the unwanted variation factors estimated by RUVs to the sample metadata (colData). Next, we prepare for differential expression by creating an EdgeR DGEList object and calculating normalization factors. We then filter out genes with low expression, keeping only those with sufficient counts across conditions to ensure robust differential testing.


Code
# Add estimated unwanted variation factors to sample metadata
colData(ca1do) <- cbind.DataFrame(colData(ca1do), ruvs$W, returnOnly = TRUE)

# Create DGEList for EdgeR analysis and calculate normalization factors
y <- DGEList(counts(ca1do), samples = colData(ca1do))
y1 <- calcNormFactors(y, method = "upperquartile")

# Filter out lowly expressed genes to improve statistical power
keep <- filterByExpr(y, group = ca1do$condition, min.count = 5, min.total.count = 0)
keep.genes <- data.frame(keep[keep == "TRUE"])
ca1do <- ca1do[rownames(keep.genes), ]




Differential expression analysis with EdgeR and result annotation
We perform differential expression analysis using EdgeR, specifying contrasts of interest and incorporating the unwanted variation factors as covariates. After obtaining results, we annotate the differential expression results with gene symbols and Ensembl IDs for interpretability.


Code
# Run differential expression analysis with EdgeR using condition contrasts and RUVs factors
cntrs <- c("SD - HC")
reslist <- applyEdgeR(counts = counts(ca1do),
                      colData = colData(ca1do),
                      factors = "condition",
                      wnames = colnames(ruvs$W),
                      contrasts = cntrs,
                      p.threshold = 1,
                      edgeroffs = log(y1$samples$lib.size * y1$samples$norm.factors))

# Annotate DE results with gene symbols and Ensembl IDs
newpshitsl <- newpshits[, c(2, 1)]
reslist <- lapply(reslist, function(r) {
  r$gene <- rownames(r)
  r$ensembl <- rowData(ca1do)$TENxEnsembl[match(r$gene, rownames(rowData(ca1do)))]
  return(r)
})




Plotting results and summarizing DEGs
We visualize the differential expression results with volcano plots highlighting positive controls, and histograms of p-values to check statistical distributions. We then summarize the number of significant DEGs and count how many positive and negative control genes are detected as differentially expressed.
Then, we add logical flags to indicate which genes are significantly differentially expressed and which correspond to positive control genes. Finally, we attach the full differential expression results back to the dataset’s row metadata for further use or export.


Code
# Volcano plot to visualize DEGs and positive control genes
luciaVolcanoPlot1(reslist[[1]],
                  positive.controls.df = newpshitsl,
                  prefix = paste0(names(reslist)[1]),
                  threshold = 0.05) + theme_bw()

title: Differential Expression of Shank3 DeltaC of CA1-do
text:
Code
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, include=TRUE,cache=FALSE)



Loading required libraries


Code
library(scater)
library(edgeR)
library(RUVSeq)
library(darioscripts)
library(DT)
library(ggpubr)
source("../R/luciavolcano.R")
library(muscat)
library(biomaRt)




Pseudo-bulk data construction for differential analysis
In this code chunk, we construct pseudo-bulk RNA-seq data from single-cell multiome datasets using the TENxMultiomeTools package. Specifically, we:

Load a list of SingleCellExperiment objects (scelist) representing multiple samples.
Aggregate the single-cell count data across cell labels (using aggregateAcrossCells) to simulate bulk RNA-seq profiles for each annotated group.
Generate a combined SingleCellExperiment object (scepseudo) by merging the pseudo-bulk profiles from all samples.
Save the resulting pseudo-bulk dataset to an RDS file for downstream analysis.

This step is performed to prepare the data for differential expression analysis, which is more robust when applied to aggregated (pseudo-bulk) counts rather than single-cell counts.

Note: This code chunk is not evaluated in the document for time-saving purposes. Instead, we directly start from the pre-computed results stored in the GEX_pseudo_2023.RDS file.



Code
scelist <- readRDS("~/Downloads/multiome_data/data/scelist_SR_dbl_signacfilt_dimred_noATAC_doublrm.RDS")

library(TENxMultiomeTools)
scelistpseudo <- lapply(scelist, function(sce)
{
    scea <- aggregateAcrossCells(sce, use.assay.type="counts",
        id=DataFrame(label=sce$labels))
    colnames(scea) <- paste(scea$label, scea$replicate, scea$condition, scea$genotype, sep="_")
    scea
})

scepseudo <- cbind(scelistpseudo[[1]], scelistpseudo[[2]], scelistpseudo[[3]],
                   scelistpseudo[[4]], scelistpseudo[[5]], scelistpseudo[[6]],
                   scelistpseudo[[7]], scelistpseudo[[8]], scelistpseudo[[9]],
                   scelistpseudo[[10]], scelistpseudo[[11]], scelistpseudo[[12]])

saveRDS(scepseudo, file="~/Downloads/multiome_data/data/GEX_pseudo_2023.RDS")




Loading and annotating pseudo-bulk data for differential analysis
In this code chunk, we load the previously computed pseudo-bulk gene expression dataset and perform sample- and gene-level annotations in preparation for differential expression analysis. The steps include:

Loading data:

The pseudo-bulk dataset is read from the RDS file GEX_pseudo_2023.RDS.
A composite variable gcondition is created by concatenating genotype and condition.
Each sample is annotated with a high-level cell class (superclass) based on the label, distinguishing non-neuronal, glutamatergic, and GABAergic neuronal populations.

Annotating negative controls:

A set of known negative control genes is loaded and split into training and testing subsets (90% and 10%, respectively).
Genes in the pseudo-bulk dataset are flagged as negative controls (negctl) or test negative controls (negctltest) accordingly.

Annotating positive controls:

Known positive control genes are loaded from an external file and flagged in the dataset (posctl).
Their presence in the dataset is also recorded in a kept column.

Filtering samples:

The dataset is restricted to samples from the Shank3 DeltaC (S3) genotype only.




Code
multiome <- readRDS("~/Downloads/multiome_data/data/GEX_pseudo_2023.RDS") # pseudobulk


multiome$gcondition <- paste(multiome$genotype, multiome$condition, sep="_")

multiome$superclass <- "Non Neuronal"

multiome$superclass[multiome$label %in% c("CA1-do","CA1-ProS", "CA2", "CA3", "SUB-ProS", "DG")] <- "Neuronal - Glutamatergic"
multiome$superclass[multiome$label %in% c("Lamp5", "Sncg", "Vip", "Serpinf1",
                                          "Ntng1", "Pvalb", "Sst", "Sst-Chodl")] <-
    "Neuronal - Gabaergic"


nc <- readRDS("~/Downloads/multiome_data/ctrls/SD_neg_ctrl.RDS")
dim(nc)


[1] 4033    2


Code
rowData(multiome)$negctl <- FALSE
rowData(multiome)$negctl[rownames(multiome) %in% nc$symbol] <- TRUE
rm(.Random.seed, envir=globalenv())
set.seed(3)
idxsamp <- sample(seq_along(nc$ensembl_id), round((dim(nc)[1]*10)/100))
nctest <- nc[idxsamp,]
nc <- nc[-idxsamp,]
rowData(multiome)$negctl <- FALSE
rowData(multiome)$negctl[rownames(multiome) %in% nc$symbol] <- TRUE
rowData(multiome)$negctltest <- FALSE
rowData(multiome)$negctltest[rownames(multiome) %in% nctest$symbol] <- TRUE


newps <- read.table("~/Downloads/multiome_data/ctrls/111022_Positive_Controls_from_BMC_Genomics_AddFile2.txt", header=TRUE)
newpshits <- newps
rowData(multiome)$posctl <- FALSE
rowData(multiome)$posctl[rownames(multiome) %in% newps$Gene_Name] <- TRUE

newpshits$kept <- FALSE
newpshits$kept[which(newpshits$Gene_Name %in% rownames(multiome))] <- TRUE
multiome <- multiome[,multiome$genotype=="S3"]
multiome$condition[multiome$condition=="CTRL"] <- "HC"




Annotating genes with reference metadata
In this code chunk, we enrich the pseudo-bulk dataset with gene-level annotations using an external reference table. The steps performed are:

A reference table (features_duplicates.tsv) containing gene metadata (such as gene symbols, Ensembl IDs, chromosome locations, and genomic coordinates) is loaded.
Genes in the pseudo-bulk dataset are matched with entries in the reference table based on gene symbols.
For matched genes, the following annotations are added to the rowData of the multiome object:

TENxSymbol: official 10x Genomics gene symbol
TENxEnsembl: Ensembl gene ID
TENxChr: chromosome
TENxStart: transcription start coordinate
TENxEnd: transcription end coordinate


This metadata is useful for downstream analysis and interpretation of differential expression results.


Code
feat <- read.table("~/Downloads/multiome_data/reference/features_duplicates.tsv", sep="\t", header=TRUE)
rn <- rownames(rowData(multiome)) 
idx <- which(rn %in% feat$symbol)
idx1 <- which(feat$symbol %in% rn)
rowData(multiome)$TENxSymbol[idx] <- feat$symbol[idx1]
rowData(multiome)$TENxEnsembl[idx] <- feat$ensembl[idx1]
rowData(multiome)$TENxChr[idx] <- feat$chr[idx1]
rowData(multiome)$TENxStart[idx] <- feat$start[idx1]
rowData(multiome)$TENxEnd[idx] <- feat$end[idx1]




Exploratory analysis of raw (non-normalized) data
In this code chunk, we explore the structure of the raw (non-normalized) pseudo-bulk counts for the "CA1-do" cell population using dimensionality reduction techniques:

Principal Component Analysis (PCA):

A PCA is computed on the log-transformed raw counts (log1p(counts(...))).
The PCA plot distinguishes samples by condition using different colors and shapes.
The function plotPCAs is used to generate the plot with cowplot styling, and color/shape mappings are customized.

Normalization:

Log-normalization is then applied using logNormCounts normalization to prepare the data for subsequent analyses.


This step provides a visual assessment of variability in the raw data and sets up the object for normalized downstream analyses.


Code
ca1do <- multiome[,multiome$label=="CA1-do"]
plot.dir <- "~/Downloads/multiome_data/plots/"

plotPCAs(log1p(counts(ca1do)),
         colData=colData(ca1do),
         shapeBy="condition",
         colorBy="condition", cowplot=TRUE, prefix="log(raw-counts) CA1-do",
         returnOnly=TRUE, size=3) +
        scale_color_manual(values=c("red", "black")) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = 16:17) + 
    theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "none")







Data subsetting, upper-quartile normalization, and PCA visualization
First, we apply upper-quartile normalization to account for sequencing depth differences across samples. After normalization, we perform a PCA on the log-transformed normalized counts to visualize how samples cluster by their condition, which helps assess batch effects or biological differences.


Code
ca1do <- multiome[,multiome$labels=="CA1-do"]

uq <- EDASeq::betweenLaneNormalization(counts(ca1do), which="upper")

plotPCAs(log1p(uq),
         colData=colData(ca1do),
         shapeBy="condition",
         colorBy="condition", cowplot=TRUE, prefix="log(UQ)",
         returnOnly=TRUE, size=3) +
        scale_color_manual(values=c("red", "black")) + 
        scale_shape_manual(values = 16:17) + 
    theme_bw()







RUVs normalization and PCA visualization
To remove unwanted variation not captured by the condition (e.g., batch effects), we apply RUVs normalization using a set of negative control genes. We define sample groups by condition and use k=3 factors to adjust. The normalized counts from RUVs are stored, and a PCA is again performed on these adjusted counts to check if unwanted variation was reduced.


Code
grp <- makeGroups(ca1do$condition)
rownames(grp) <- unique(ca1do$condition)

k=3
ruvs <- RUVs(x=round(as.matrix(uq)), cIdx=rownames(ca1do)[rowData(ca1do)$negctl],
             k=k, scIdx=grp, round=TRUE)
assays(ca1do)$uqruvsk3 <- ruvs$normalizedCounts
assays(ca1do)$loguqruvsk3 <- log1p(ruvs$normalizedCounts)

plotPCAs(log1p(ruvs$normalizedCounts),
         colData=colData(ca1do),
         shapeBy="condition",
         colorBy="condition", cowplot=TRUE, prefix=paste0("WT log(UQ+RUVsk",k,")"),
         returnOnly=TRUE, size=3) +
        scale_color_manual(values=c("red", "black")) + 
    scale_shape_manual(values = 16:17) + 
    theme_bw()







Add RUVs factors to sample metadata and filter genes
We append the unwanted variation factors estimated by RUVs to the sample metadata (colData). Next, we prepare for differential expression by creating an EdgeR DGEList object and calculating normalization factors. We then filter out genes with low expression, keeping only those with sufficient counts across conditions to ensure robust differential testing.


Code
colData(ca1do) <- cbind.DataFrame(colData(ca1do), ruvs$W, returnOnly=TRUE)

y <- DGEList(counts(ca1do), samples=colData(ca1do))
y1 <- calcNormFactors(y, method="upperquartile")
keep <- filterByExpr(y, group=ca1do$condition, min.count=5, min.total.count=0)
keep.genes <- data.frame(keep[keep=="TRUE"])
ca1do <- ca1do[rownames(keep.genes),]




Differential expression analysis with EdgeR and result annotation
We perform differential expression analysis using EdgeR, specifying contrasts of interest and incorporating the unwanted variation factors as covariates. After obtaining results, we annotate the differential expression results with gene symbols and Ensembl IDs for interpretability.


Code
cntrs <- c("SD - HC")
reslist <- applyEdgeR(counts=counts(ca1do), colData=colData(ca1do),
                      factors="condition", wnames=colnames(ruvs$W),
                      contrasts=cntrs, p.threshold=1,
                      edgeroffs=log(y1$samples$lib.size*y1$samples$norm.factors))


newpshitsl <- newpshits[,c(2,1)]
reslist <- lapply(reslist, function(r)
{ 
    r$gene <- rownames(r)
    r$ensembl <- rowData(ca1do)$TENxEnsembl[match(r$gene, rownames(rowData(ca1do)))]
    return(r) 
})




Plotting results and summarizing DEGs
We visualize the differential expression results with volcano plots highlighting positive controls, and histograms of p-values to check statistical distributions. We then summarize the number of significant DEGs and count how many positive and negative control genes are detected as differentially expressed.
Then, we add logical flags to indicate which genes are significantly differentially expressed and which correspond to positive control genes. Finally, we attach the full differential expression results back to the dataset’s row metadata for further use or export.


Code
luciaVolcanoPlot1(reslist[[1]], positive.controls.df=newpshitsl,
                      prefix=paste0(names(reslist)[1]), threshold=0.05) + theme_bw()

                     show.plot.flag=FALSE) + theme_bw() + ggtitle("SD-HC P-Value Histogram")

{
    r <- r[r$FDR<0.05,]
    sum(tolower(rownames(r)) %in% tolower(newpshits$Gene_Name))
}))

{

    sum(tolower(rownames(r)) %in% tolower(nc$symbol))
}))

    r <- reslist[[i]]

    r$sign[r$FDR<0.05] <- TRUE
    r$poscont <- FALSE
    r$poscont[tolower(rownames(r)) %in% tolower(newpshits$Gene_Name)] <- TRUE

For each cell type: - The function statDEG() summarizes DEG statistics, likely counting the number of significant genes. - These summaries are collected into a combined table with buildTab(), which returns a data.frame containing at least:
